relations.myth: The two powers at the gate
relations.note: Kalfou sits opposite Legba, dividing nocturnal intercardinal forces from Legba’s daylight cardinal authority.
Métraux classifies Maître Carrefour as Legba-Petwo, the magically potent Petwo manifestation of Legba.
At midnight Kalfou and Gran Bwa jointly govern magical practice with Baron Cimetière.
Kalfou and Baron Cimetière join Gran Bwa in the midnight triad patronizing magicians.
Maître Carrefour and Baron Maître Cimetière appear together in secret-society ceremonial accounts.
Simbi sometimes joins Kalfou, Gede, and Gran Bwa in governing forces required for magic.

relations.myth: Governance of magic and the dead
relations.note: Gede governs dealings with the dead while Kalfou governs dangerous nocturnal passage.
Kalfou and Bosou are both served by reported Makaya, Bizango, and Sanpwel groups.
Kalfou and Ezili Dantò are both served by reported Makaya, Bizango, and Sanpwel groups.
Kalfou and Danbala Laflanbo are both served by reported Makaya, Bizango, and Sanpwel groups.
Kalfou and Simityè are both served by reported Makaya, Bizango, and Sanpwel groups.
The Haitian Kalfou complex is reconstructed as a differentiation within the older Fon Legba crossroads tradition.
Comparable messenger and crossroads powers encouraged scholarly comparison and partial Atlantic fusion.
Christian polemic identifies Kalfou with the Devil, although Vodou classifies him as a lwa.
Modern comparativists analogize Hecate and Kalfou through their associations with crossroads.
Modern comparativists analogize Hermes and Kalfou through mediation and crossroads symbolism.
Modern comparativists analogize Pandora and Kalfou through the release of misfortune.
Contemporary devotional and commercial sources sometimes identify Saint Andrew with Kalfou.
Contemporary devotional and commercial sources sometimes identify Saint Anthony the Hermit with Kalfou.
Contemporary devotional and commercial sources sometimes identify Saint Michael with Kalfou.
Contemporary devotional and commercial sources sometimes identify Saint Expedite with Kalfou.
